evidence_items.locator: Section 5, limitations of data collection; Appendix A.4
evidence_items.explanation: The developer reports that roughly 96% of its instruction dataset was classified as English, possibly more because of classifier errors. This directly supports English predominance in instruction tuning, without treating that percentage as the pretraining distribution.

evidence_items.publisher: Liang et al., Stanford CRFM, arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Section 3.1, Languages; introduction's description of the 16 core scenarios
evidence_items.explanation: HELM's initial core scenarios covered only English, including different English varieties. The authors explicitly say that even multilingual BLOOM was evaluated only for English.

evidence_items.publisher: Srivastava et al., BIG-bench collaboration, arXiv

receipt.public_excerpt: a handful also target lower-resource languages

evidence_items.explanation: BIG-bench documents limited lower-resource-language coverage and reports that its BIG-G training mixture contained about 6% non-English text. Its multilingual tasks also show that English predominance coexisted with deliberate efforts to test other languages.

BLOOM was trained on 46 natural languages, and the project developed a multilingual prompted dataset collection. These are substantial exceptions to an English-only description, but do not negate predominance in other prominent systems and evaluations.

unresolved_gaps: The selected sources do not provide a census of every model or benchmark.
Dataset composition alone does not establish the size of a cross-language reasoning-performance gap.
